passed.result: A single cooperative scheduler owns normal fake audit and protected fixture work. Fair rotation and bounded-aging tests passed without a global task lock or permanent starvation.

ConflictKey creation CAS, control CAS and idempotency, pause-resume-cancel boundaries, shared fake OCR single-producer behavior, cancellation isolation, and zero heavy-resource leases while waiting_user all passed.

The pause-boundary defect found during review was fixed. Every WorkItem whose status changed had a strictly newer record version and a matching work_item.changed event; resource projection changes also advanced the event cursor.

Old and partial temporary schemas are rejected through the read-only pre-WAL gate. Protected test fixtures remain disabled by default, use only fake adapters when enabled, and keep BusinessOutcome empty.

The console displayed four tasks together with independent selection and controls. Problem items did not block normal work, and cancellation confirmation showed the task, scope, retained-result rule, and unprocessed-item rule.
Loop 4 production evidence transactions, process supervision, heartbeat, and production crash takeover were not implemented early.

non_blocking.risk: The independent four-task browser run produced about 180 dynamic requests, mostly repeated jobs and resources reads. Before a real 30-waybill shadow run, coalesce event-triggered refreshes and avoid rewriting waiting_resource rows when their visible state did not change.
The resource overview reports only a count of active task steps; a later diagnostic view should show the holder identity and held duration.
A successful loading probe still uses the generic phrase that shadow audit completed; use loading-probe-specific completion text in a later copy pass.
Runner supervision, heartbeat, and takeover of leases left active by a process crash remain intentionally deferred to the Loop 4 evidence and recovery contract.
